speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a psychiatric history and a new movement disorder; to help me understand what is happening, can you tell me exactly what movements you are experiencing and when they started?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old college student. The patient is here for a follow-up appointment. He was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and started on risperidone approximately 2 months ago. Reports a significant improvement in psychiatric symptoms since the start of treatment.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is excellent news regarding your psychiatric improvement. However, since you are on risperidone, I need to know if these new movements are involuntary (like tremors, stiffness, or repetitive motions) or if they are side effects like feeling restless (akathisia). When exactly did these movements start relative to starting the medication?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inability to remain still, persistent feeling of restlessness. I also have Frequent fidgeting, Repetitive crossing and uncrossing of legs, Pacing.

speaker: Doctor
text: The symptoms of persistent restlessness, fidgeting, and an inability to sit still strongly suggest akathisia, a common side effect of risperidone. Have you noticed any muscle stiffness, tremors, or difficulty moving your limbs as well? Additionally, have you experienced any changes in your mood, such as irritability or anxiety?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Recently diagnosed with schizophrenia. No other significant past medical history. Social history: College student, lives with parents. Denies tobacco, alcohol, or drug use.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Drug-induced akathisia secondary to risperidone therapy. The clinical presentation of subjective inner restlessness and objective motor behaviors like fidgeting and pacing, occurring two months after initiating risperidone, is highly characteristic of this condition.
